The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 9(B) / 2009-10 dated 02.06.2023 pertaining to Sy. No. 11/1A/1A/1A measuring 3864 Sq. feet (1012 Sq. Meters) of Makali village, Dasanapura Hobli.
A.P. No.30/2023 .2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 3864 Sq. feet (1012 Sq. Meters) in Sy. No. 11/1A/1A/1A of Makali village, Dasanapura Hobli has been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No. 2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.2000 (E) dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1)
and (2) vide S.O. No. 1923(E) dated 13.11.2007.

The respondent No.2 has passed the award on 10.04.2008 and determined the market value of agricultural lands at Rs. 35 lakhs per acre and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.3,09,120/-, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 02.09.2009 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-4/CR/9(A), 9(B) & 11/2009-10 dated 02.06.2023.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The petitioner claims that the respondent No.2 has grossly erred in not following the provisions of NH Act i.e., Section 3G(7)(a), the substantive law while passing the impugned award, which is contrary to the provisions of Section 28 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the respondent No.2 by placing reliance upon the aforesaid notification has observed that the guidance value of NA lands abutting NH is Rs.

Further the market value awarded by the respondent No.2 is 9.2 times higher than that of the amount fixed by the respondent No.3 which is imply exorbitant.
The respondent No.2 A.P. No.30/2023
has relied upon a subsequent notification and awarded additional 50% and 25% which is completely arbitrary.
There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently the same is liable to be set aside under Section 34(2A) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .9. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri. H.C.
Puttaswamigowda is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.11/1A1A1A measuring 3864 Sq. feet (1012 Sq. Meters) of Makali village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification dated 13.11.2007
, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the A.P. No.30/2023 respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.175/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs. 3,09,120/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.
.10.

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Sri. H.C. Puttaswamigowda filed an application on 02.09.2009 before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 5,000/- per Sq. feet.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-4/CR/ 9(A), 9(B) &
11/2009-10 dated 02.06.2023.

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.657/- per Sq. feet i.e., guidance value of NH lands abutting NH is Rs. 425/- per Sq. feet and the respondent No.2 added 50% and 25% on the guidance value and also the SLAO determined and paid A.P. No.30/2023

the compensation per Sq. feet is Rs.86/- (75% of Rs.425/-
determined the compensation in respect of agricultural land) .11.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on 22.11.2006.
As such, the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 17.04.2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 4 months from the date of A.P. No.30/2023 publication of Preliminary Notification.

It is true that as per the NH Act,
the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.12. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs.
National Highways Authority of India.

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.

However, in the case on hand, such A.P. No.30/2023 notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.
.13.

In the case on hand, the respondent No.1 claimed that proper award has been passed and no such case has been made out by the petitioner to intervene with the award passed by the respondent No.
2.

When the respondent No. 1 claimed that the respondent No. 2 has passed the order or order is in accordance with law, then it is for the respondent No. 1 to show that the order passed by the respondent No. 2 is in accordance with law and said order has been passed by following all procedure contemplated under law.

.14. Admittedly, the respondent No. 2 has enhanced the compensation from Rs. 175/- to Rs.425/-
per Square feet, which is almost 75% of the market value determined by the LAO.

Hence, it is for the respondent No. 1 to substantiate the fact that the market value of the acquired property is Rs. 425/-
per Square feet and not Rs. 175/- per Square feet or it is for A.P. No.30/2023 the petitioner to show that by considering the relevant documents, the respondent No. 2 has enhanced the market value of the acquired property and thereby awarded compensation.
.15.

It is the claim of the petitioner in the petition that as per the Special Instructions to the notification dated 17.04.2007, it provides that the properties adjacent to National and State Highways for which rates have not been fixed in the rate list, additional rate of 50% and 25% of other properties shall be fixed respectively and claimed that if the rate is not fixed for the properties adjacent to the properties of National Highways, the Arbitrator can enhance the price at 50% and in case of State Highways, additional rate of 25% can be fixed but 75% cannot be enhanced.
The claim of the petitioner is that the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 enhanced 75% of the market value, which is not permissible and accordingly claimed that the enhancement cannot be accepted.

Admittedly,
the SLAO fixed the market value to the acquired property is A.P. No.30/2023 Rs. 175/- and that has been enhanced to Rs.425/- per Sq. feet.
If the said enhancement is accepted, certainly it is clear that the respondent No. 2 enhanced the market value to the tune of 75%.
Hence, it is for the Arbitrator to give explanation on what basis 75% of the market value has been enhanced.

5 .16.

sentences.text: The only reason assigned by the respondent No. 2 for enhancement of 75% is the discretion but it is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used judicially or not arbitrarily.

Admittedly as observed by the respondent No. 2 in its order as well as claimed by the petitioner in the petition that the Arbitrator can enhance 50% of the market value, if the market value of the acquired property exists beside the National Highways is not found in or fixed in the rate list.
As such, only 50% of the market value can be enhanced by the SLAO and not more than that.
If the Arbitrator has enhanced the compensation by adding another 25%, then the total enhancement comes to 75%.
If the arbitrator enhance the compensation by adding both A.P. No.30/2023 50% and 25% then there must be special reason why the Arbitrator is enhancing 75% of the market value.
Such reasons are not found in the order of the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2.
When such a case, certainly said enhancement cannot be accepted.

It is also not made out by the respondent No. 2 in its order that the property of respondent No. 1 has been acquired, has not found in the rate list, as such, the Arbitrator has added additional rate of 50% along with 25%.
Further the value of the property has been enhanced as per the notification of the year 2007, which is also not the part of records received from the Arbitrator.
Further, no such case is made out by the respondent No. 1 before the respondent No. 2 in the Arbitration proceedings.

Therefore, it is clear that the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal and against the statutory provisions of Substantive Law that is in force and the award passed by the Arbitrator also leads to draw adverse inference under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act as the documents relied A.P. No.30/2023 by the Arbitrator not found in the records received from the Arbitrator.

The Arbitrator relied on the guidance value of the year 2007 that came to effect from 01.04.2007 and the land involved in this acquired one year prior to the said date and also the Arbitrator has not given any specific reason for enhancement of 25% as claimed in the year.
As such, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal.
It is well settled principle of law that if the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal, then such award should be set aside.

As discussed early, as the respondent No. 1 though supported the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 has not placed any materials to substantiate enhancement made by the Arbitrator to the acquired property.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator/respondent No. 2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 9(B) / 2009-10 pertaining to Sy.
No.11/1A1A1A measuring 3864 Sq. feet (1012 Sq. Meters) of Makali village, Dasanapura Hobli. is set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
